decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Metagross. Lead Incineroar+Metagross provides Intimidate support, Fake Out disruption, and Mega Metagross offensive pressure. Incineroar's Darkest Lariat hits Gengar super-effectively while Meteor Mash threatens Aerodactyl. Mamoswine backline handles Dragonite with 4x Ice Shard priority after Multiscale breaks. decisions.notebook: Opponent has Mega Gengar (Shadow Tag trap threat), Aerodactyl (Tailwind/Rock Slide), Dragonite (Multiscale), Clefable (Follow Me), Arcanine (Intimidate), Empoleon (Competitive). Plan: Use Intimidate pivots and priority to manage Dragonite's Multiscale. Mega Metagross with Tough Claws is primary win condition. Mamoswine Ice Shard breaks Dragonite after Multiscale. Rotom-Heat handles Water/Steel types. Hatterene TR backup if speed control needed. Watch for Clefable Follow Me redirecting key attacks. Aerodactyl Focus Sash can be broken with Fake Out.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Turn-one job: Gengar Mega Evolves to establish Shadow Tag trap while Aerodactyl provides fast Tailwind or Wide Guard (blocking Mamoswine EQ/Rock Slide and Hatterene Gleam) to secure immediate tempo. Backline: Empoleon deters Incineroar Intimidate switches with Competitive while checking Ice/Fairy moves; Dragonite provides Multiscale bulk and Extreme Speed priority for late-game cleanup.
decisions.notebook: Matchup Plan: Mega Gengar traps defensive and Fairy/Psychic pieces with Shadow Tag. Aerodactyl provides fast speed control and Wide Guard vs spread move users (Mamoswine, Hatterene). Empoleon deters Intimidate core (Incineroar). Dragonite offers physical priority and Multiscale stability.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out breaks Aerodactyl's Focus Sash at priority +3, guaranteeing Meteor Mash KO next turn. Metagross Protect blocks Gengar's Shadow Ball (43-140% OHKO range). Incineroar tanks one Rock Slide but has Sitrus Berry recovery. This safely removes the Tailwind/Rock Slide threat while preserving Metagross for the Mega sweep.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl leads with Focus Sash + Unnerve; break sash turn 1 to enable guaranteed Meteor Mash KO. Gengar Timid with Shadow Ball is primary Metagross threat - Protect or switch to avoid. Mega Metagross Tough Claws is win condition; preserve HP. Intimidate already applied (-1 Atk to both foes). Watch for opponent switching to Clefable Follow Me or Dragonite Multiscale. Mamoswine Ice Shard breaks Dragonite after Multiscale loss. Rotom-Heat handles Empoleon.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 178 Speed cleanly outspeeds both opposing active Pokémon, including Mega Metagross (max 162). Shadow Ball from Mega Gengar deals 67.9-120% to Metagross, threatening an immediate KO or heavy pressure while activating Shadow Tag. Aerodactyl uses Tailwind to secure team-wide speed advantage, backed by its Focus Sash if Fake Out is directed elsewhere.
decisions.notebook: Matchup Plan: Mega Gengar traps defensive/Psychic cores with Shadow Tag. Aerodactyl provides speed control and Wide Guard support. Empoleon checks Intimidate, Dragonite provides multiscale priority.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega outspeeds and threatens Metagross with 2x Shadow Ball. Protect guarantees Metagross survival while Incineroar's Darkest Lariat pressures Gengar (SE 2x). Aerodactyl's Focus Sash remains at 91% HP - we'll break it next turn with Meteor Mash after Gengar is weakened or forced out. This avoids risking Metagross KO while applying offensive pressure. Mega Evolution saved for safer timing.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl leads Focus Sash + Unnerve; must break sash before guaranteed Meteor Mash KO. Gengar Timid Shadow Ball is primary Metagross threat - Protect or switch mandatory. Mega Metagross Tough Claws is win condition; preserve HP. Both foes outspeed our leads significantly. Watch for Clefable FollowMe switch or Dragonite Multiscale. Mamoswine Ice Shard breaks Dragonite post-Multiscale. Rotom-Heat handles Empoleon. Intimidate already applied turn 1.

decisions.rationale: Metagross cannot use Protect safely again and is trapped by Shadow Tag alongside Incineroar. Gengar-Mega outspeeds both foes natively and hits Mega Metagross for 67.9-120% with Shadow Ball. Aerodactyl sets Tailwind before taking potential damage, guaranteeing speed control for the entire team against backline threats like Meowscarada.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Incineroar + Metagross against Gengar + Aerodactyl. Metagross revealed Protect, Incineroar revealed Fake Out. Shadow Tag traps non-Ghost foes on field.

decisions.rationale: Empoleon is the optimal switch-in as it quad-resists Metagross's entire revealed attacking toolkit (Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch, Ice Punch) and resists dark/fire coverage cleanly. Dragonite would take quad-effective damage from Metagross's Ice Punch, breaking Multiscale or risking an immediate KO. Empoleon's Competitive ability also deters Incineroar's Parting Shot under Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Incineroar + Metagross. Metagross has Protect, Ice Punch, Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch. Incineroar has Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz.

decisions.rationale: Aerodactyl at 91% with broken Focus Sash must be eliminated to remove Tailwind and Rock Slide spread threat. Mega Metagross Meteor Mash (87.7-209%) + Incineroar Darkest Lariat (27.3-65.8%) guarantees KO on Aerodactyl even at minimum rolls. Both foes outspeed, so Incineroar risks Hydro Pump OHKO (47.5-156.5%), but removing Aerodactyl is priority. Darkest Lariat preferred over Flare Blitz (NVE 18.7-45.8%).
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl Focus Sash already broken turn 1; Tailwind active 3 turns. Gengar-Mega fainted. Empoleon Competitive punishes Intimidate/Parting Shot - avoid targeting it with stat drops. Mega Metagross Tough Claws is primary win condition; preserve HP. Mamoswine Ice Shard breaks Dragonite Multiscale. Rotom-Heat Thunderbolt 4x vs Empoleon Water/Steel. Incineroar Sitrus Berry at 100%. Opponent has Clefable FollowMe and Dragonite Multiscale in reserve - plan for late-game switches.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Heat's Thunderbolt is 4x super effective vs Empoleon's Water/Steel typing, likely securing a KO. Metagross-Mega's Steel moves are all 0.25x vs Empoleon, making it ineffective to attack. Rotom resists Hydro Pump (0.5x) and takes neutral Flash Cannon. Empoleon's Tailwind-boosted Speed means it moves first, but Rotom can survive and retaliate. Mamoswine is slower and Earthquake is only 2x, making Rotom the superior switch-in.
decisions.notebook: Rotom-Heat Thunderbolt 4x vs Empoleon Water/Steel is primary removal tool. Metagross-Mega struggles vs Water/Steel; preserve for late-game vs Fairy/Dragon. Opponent Tailwind grants massive Speed advantage for 3 turns. Clefable FollowMe and Dragonite Multiscale are key late-game threats requiring Mamoswine Ice Shard to break Multiscale. Empoleon Competitive punishes Intimidate/Parting Shot - avoid stat drops. Arcanine Intimidate + Charcoal Flare Blitz is a threat to Metagross. Plan endgame around preserving Metagross HP and using Mamoswine priority for Dragonite.

decisions.rationale: Empoleon under Tailwind outspeeds Incineroar and base Metagross, dealing 71-128% to Incineroar with Hydro Pump. Empoleon heavily resists Metagross's Steel/Ice coverage (0.25x). Rock Slide applies spread pressure and flinch chances. If Incineroar uses Parting Shot into Empoleon, Competitive will trigger +2 SpA.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Rotom Protects to avoid 4x Earthquake OHKO (58-192%). Metagross Ice Punch breaks Dragonite's Multiscale (78.8-171.1% but halved to 39-86%). Metagross survives single-target EQ (26-78%) and likely Hydro Pump (22-74%). Next turn: Tailwind expires, Multiscale broken, Metagross Ice Punch guarantees Dragonite KO, Rotom Thunderbolts Empoleon (56-122%).
decisions.notebook: Thunderbolt is 2x vs Empoleon Water/Steel (not 4x). Ice Punch cannot OHKO Dragonite through Multiscale at full HP—must break Multiscale first. Earthquake 4x vs Rotom is the primary threat; Protect is essential when Dragonite is active. Metagross struggles vs Water/Steel types; preserve for late-game vs Dragon/Fairy. Mamoswine Ice Shard priority is key for breaking Multiscale and finishing weakened Dragonite. Empoleon Competitive punishes stat drops—avoid Parting Shot/Intimidate. Tailwind grants opponent 2 turns of Speed control; plan around moving last. Arcanine Intimidate+Charcoal Flare Blitz threatens Metagross if brought.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, both Dragonite (264 Effective Speed) and Empoleon (160 Effective Speed) outspeed Rotom-Heat (max 138). Double targeting Rotom-Heat with Dragon Claw and Hydro Pump guarantees a KO before it can move. Multiscale allows Dragonite to easily survive an Ice Punch from Metagross-Mega, and Lum Berry protects against potential status like Will-O-Wisp or Freeze.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Incineroar + Metagross. Metagross has Protect, Ice Punch, Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch. Incineroar has Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz. Rotom-Heat has Levitate, Leftovers, Thunderbolt, Overheat, Will-O-Wisp, Protect.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch's +1 priority KOs 8% HP Dragonite before it acts, completely neutralizing the Earthquake threat. Protect shields Rotom from Empoleon's Hydro Pump. Even if Protect fails (33%), Dragonite is already KOed by priority Bullet Punch, leaving only Empoleon. Ice Punch would let Dragonite move first under Tailwind, risking a 4x Earthquake on Rotom.
decisions.notebook: Bullet Punch +1 priority reliably KOs heavily weakened Dragonite before it can act, eliminating Earthquake threat entirely. Protect success rate drops to 33% after consecutive use—factor this into risk assessment. Empoleon Competitive punishes any stat drops (Intimidate, Parting Shot); avoid completely. Tailwind grants opponent 2 turns of Speed advantage; plan to use priority moves or Protect to compensate. Metagross struggles vs Water/Steel (Empoleon resists all Steel moves 0.25x); preserve for late-game vs Dragon/Fairy types. Mamoswine Ice Shard +1 priority is key backup for breaking Multiscale and finishing Dragonite. Rotom-Heat's Levitate grants Ground immunity but Earthquake still hits via spread mechanics in doubles.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Dragonite's priority +2 Extreme Speed lands on Rotom-Heat before Metagross can target Dragonite with Bullet Punch (+1). Empoleon's Hydro Pump (160 effective Speed) then easily finishes Rotom-Heat before Rotom can fire Thunderbolt. Once Rotom-Heat is eliminated, Empoleon (at 100% HP) quad-resists Metagross's entire revealed movepool (Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch, Ice Punch) and easily secures Game 1.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent leads Incineroar + Metagross. Metagross-Mega has Protect, Ice Punch, Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch. Incineroar has Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz. Rotom-Heat has Levitate, Leftovers, Thunderbolt, Overheat, Will-O-Wisp, Protect. Empoleon quad-resists Metagross's entire offensive coverage.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine Earthquake is a guaranteed OHKO on Empoleon (110.5-202.5%) and outspeeds it (120 vs 80-112). Metagross's moves are all 0.25x resisted by Water/Steel Empoleon, so Protect is optimal—keeps Meta at 94% safe while Mamoswine pressures. If Empoleon Protects, we lose a turn but nothing else. If it switches, Earthquake damages the incoming threat (Arcanine neutral, Clefable neutral). This maximizes our chance to eliminate Empoleon or gain advantage on the switch-in.
decisions.notebook: Empoleon Competitive ability punishes stat drops—avoid Intimidate/Parting Shot entirely. Mamoswine Earthquake OHKOs Empoleon across all legal spreads; use as primary removal tool. Metagross-Mega Steel moves are 0.25x vs Water/Steel types—preserve for Dragon/Fairy matchups. Life Orb Mamoswine is primary win condition; protect it from super-effective special attacks (Flash Cannon, Hydro Pump). Opponent's remaining unshown Pokémon: Arcanine (Fire/Intimidate) and Clefable (Fairy/Unaware)—prepare for Intimidate switch-in and potential FollowMe redirection. Tailwind was used earlier but is now depleted. Protect success rate drops to 33% after consecutive uses—track Empoleon Protect history.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine outspeeds Empoleon (100-132 vs 80) and OHKOs with Earthquake. Protect only delays loss as Mamoswine will outspeed and KO on the following turn anyway. Our only win path is if Mamoswine refrains from using Earthquake (to avoid hitting its ally Metagross) and uses Ice Shard/Rock Slide instead, allowing Empoleon to survive and KO back with Hydro Pump.

reflections.summary: Won through efficient trading and Mamoswine’s Earthquake cleanup, but the team-preview plan was structurally flawed: bringing Rotom-Heat and Incineroar created two immediate Hydro Pump liabilities against Empoleon, and Mega Metagross offered zero Water resistance. The opponent’s reliance on Empoleon’s Hydro Pump without sustained speed control (Tailwind depleted) allowed Mamoswine to secure the win despite the preview mismatch.
reflections.adjustment: Adjust preview to lead Mamoswine with Incineroar or Metagross to immediately pressure Empoleon with Earthquake or Intimidate, completely avoiding Rotom-Heat against Water-heavy cores. If the opponent consistently pairs Empoleon with Fairy/Intimidate support, consider swapping Mega Metagross for a Water-resistant Mega or a faster pivot to neutralize Hydro Pump momentum.
reflections.notebook: Empoleon is the opponent’s primary win condition and will aggressively target Water-weak Pokémon with Hydro Pump. Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl are highly vulnerable to Incineroar’s Darkest Lariat and Metagross’s Meteor Mash. Dragonite runs Lum Berry + Multiscale; break Multiscale first, then exploit with Metagross priority. Unbrought Arcanine (Charcoal/Intimidate) and Clefable (Unaware/Follow Me) indicate a pivot/redirect strategy to protect sweepers. Mamoswine’s Earthquake is a guaranteed OHKO on Empoleon; preserve it and avoid exposing it to Hydro Pump/Flash Cannon. Tailwind is single-use; plan for speed disadvantage after early turns. Future leads must prioritize Water resistance or immediate Empoleon pressure.

reflections.summary: Bringing Mega Gengar into an Incineroar + Metagross lead backfired when Gengar was eliminated by Darkest Lariat on Turn 2 while setting Tailwind, wasting the Mega slot and leaving the backline overwhelmed by Mega Metagross and Mamoswine.
reflections.adjustment: Bench Mega Gengar in favor of leading Empoleon alongside Aerodactyl or Dragonite to punish Incineroar's Intimidate via Competitive and safely wall Mega Metagross's STAB and coverage moves.
reflections.notebook:
Opponent confirmed moves/items: Mega Metagross (Protect, Ice Punch, Meteor Mash, Bullet Punch), Incineroar (Fake Out, Darkest Lariat, Parting Shot, Flare Blitz; Sitrus Berry), Rotom-Heat (Levitate, Leftovers, Thunderbolt, Overheat, Will-O-Wisp, Protect), Mamoswine (Life Orb, Earthquake, Ice Shard, Rock Slide, Protect).
Strategic facts: Empoleon quad-resists Mega Metagross's Steel/Ice attacks and activates Competitive against Incineroar.
Plan: Lead Empoleon + Aerodactyl/Dragonite; avoid exposing fragile attackers like Gengar to Incineroar.
